resources.string: Your Nintendo Switch on this screen
Looking for a Switch on this network…
No Switch found yet. Check that the Switch is in Network mode and on the same Wi-Fi, or enter its IP.
Not connected to a Wi-Fi network.
Use an OTG adapter (USB-C to USB-A) on this device and a USB-A to USB-C cable to the Switch. A USB-C to USB-C cable does not work. The Switch must be handheld, in USB mode.
This device does not support USB OTG.
Watch what NXBeam on your PC is showing. Use the address shown in the PC window.
Fastest shows each frame the moment it arrives. Balanced and Smoothest wait a little to keep motion even on busy Wi-Fi.
Use a controller on the Switch
A controller connected to this device acts as a Switch controller while playing.
The Switch refused the connection. Is it in Network mode, and has it finished starting up?
No answer. Check that the Switch and this device are on the same network.
No Switch on USB. Plug it in and set the NXBeam overlay to USB mode.
USB access is needed. Go back and tap Connect over USB.
Another app is using the USB connection.
This NXBeam asks for a PIN.
Storage access is needed to save files
The Switch is not taking controller input. Turn on viewer input on the console.

A Switch is connected, but NXBeam is not in USB mode on it. Pick Mode USB in the NXBeam overlay and restart the Switch.
The NXBeam Switch is here. Tap Connect over USB.

This device sees nothing on USB, so it is not acting as the host. With a USB-C to USB-C cable the Switch may take that role or only charge. Use an OTG adapter (USB-C to USB-A) with a USB-A to USB-C cable.
The Switch is not among these devices. Check the cable and that the Switch is in handheld mode, with NXBeam in USB mode.
